subject: Pilot keepalive: temporary credit request while PO clears
messages:
From: Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@healthflow.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@healthflow.com
Date: 2026-11-29T09:14:00-05:00
Subject: Pilot keepalive request while PO in legal review

Hi Olga,

Quick note from my side — our legal team received the PO this morning but they flagged a couple of standard clauses and pushed it into an extra review. Procurement says the earliest sign-off looks like next week, but that timeline is not firm.

We still have a small team actively building with the sandbox and would really like to avoid the evaluation window expiring while this is being reviewed. Would Redwood be able to issue a short interim credit (48–72 hours) or a voucher to keep our pilot running until the PO clears? We can share the PO number (HF-2026-1197) and a contact in procurement if you need it.

Appreciate any flexibility — want to keep momentum on the integration work.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Meyers
Head of Engineering, Integrations | HealthFlow
jmeyers@healthflow.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachment: HealthFlow_PO_Draft.pdf (pdf)
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@healthflow.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-29T10:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Pilot keepalive request while PO in legal review

Jordan —

Thanks for the heads up and for attaching the draft. I looped Ben (sales) and Monica (billing) so we can get you a concrete option quickly. Short answer: we can offer a one-time interim credit to prevent the sandbox from lapsing while the PO is processing.

Two options we typically use:
- 72-hour guest voucher (no billing changes needed) — simplest, immediate.
- Temporary account credit applied to the trial account until PO is processed (we record in our billing system so finance can reconcile once the PO arrives).

Can you confirm which you'd prefer? If you want the temporary credit applied to the account, please confirm the exact account email for the sandbox (is it team-pilot@healthflow.com?) and the PO number to reference. If procurement needs a written confirmation from Redwood, we can provide a short email template and the voucher redline.

Ben — Monica — can you advise on the quickest internal workflow for issuing a 72-hour voucher vs. applying a short-term credit? Also flag any approvals needed if we attach credit to an account vs issuing a stand-alone voucher.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@healthflow.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-29T11:20:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Pilot keepalive request while PO in legal review

Looping in the operational steps:

We can issue a 72-hour voucher immediately — I can generate the voucher code and send it to Jordan now (no approvals required). If HealthFlow prefers the credit applied directly to the trial account, that requires a one-line finance approval but we can fast-track it (expect ~4 business hours). For the account-credit flow we'll need: account email, PO number for reconciliation, and the expected invoice amount so billing ties it back later.

Jordan — if you want the fastest unblock, I recommend the 72-hour voucher so your team doesn’t stop testing while legal and procurement finish their review. If you confirm, I’ll send the voucher code and instructions for redemption.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@healthflow.com>

If you need procurement to confirm anything in writing, loop me in and I’ll have procurement provide the name + expected sign-off date.

Appreciate the quick help.

Jordan
